statements.verbatim_passage: Model assumptions A1: The initial fire propagation rate varies linearly with temperature and wind power; A2: The target area exhibits an undulating topography, with no slope greater than 60 • ; A3: The target area contains regions of grassy marshland, secondary forest and coniferous forest; A4: The weather data are available in a timely manner.

proposal.statement: Fire propagation speed increases linearly with temperature and wind power.
proposal.passage: Model assumptions A1: The initial fire propagation rate varies linearly with temperature and wind power; A2: The target area exhibits an undulating topography, with no slope greater than 60 • ; A3: The target area contains regions of grassy marshland, secondary forest and coniferous forest; A4: The weather data are available in a timely manner.
proposal.section_key: propagation model for wildfires in the daxingan mountains

statements.verbatim_passage: A fire site with a faster propagation rate is considered to be suffering more severe fire damage and should be given a higher priority.
statements.passage_as_proposed: A fire site with a faster propagation rate is considered to be suffering more severe fire damage and should be given a higher priority.

proposal.statement: Higher fire propagation rates are considered to cause more severe fire damage and therefore receive higher priority for suppression resources.
proposal.passage: A fire site with a faster propagation rate is considered to be suffering more severe fire damage and should be given a higher priority.
proposal.impact_mechanism: higher propagation rate leads to higher priority for resource allocation
proposal.impact_outcome: allocation of suppression resources is prioritized to reduce fire damage

statements.verbatim_passage: In the case of rapid propagation (V F > 10 m/min), the rescue commanders may arrange several vehicles to transport suppression resources to each fire site to minimize total losses (Fig. 1).
statements.passage_as_proposed: In the case of rapid propagation (V F > 10 m/min), the rescue commanders may arrange several vehicles to transport suppression resources to each fire site to minimize total losses (Fig. 1).

proposal.statement: When fire propagation is rapid (greater than 10 m/min), multiple vehicles must be dispatched to each fire site to minimize total losses.
proposal.passage: In the case of rapid propagation (V F > 10 m/min), the rescue commanders may arrange several vehicles to transport suppression resources to each fire site to minimize total losses (Fig. 1).
proposal.impact_mechanism: rapid fire spread requires multiple vehicles per site
proposal.impact_outcome: reduces total losses by faster suppression

statements.verbatim_passage: When the fire propagation rate is slow (V F <= 10 m/min), the commanders may send resources to several fire sites via one vehicle (Fig. 2) (Zhang 2007;Sun et al. 2007).
statements.passage_as_proposed: When the fire propagation rate is slow (V F <= 10 m/min), the commanders may send resources to several fire sites via one vehicle (Fig. 2) (Zhang 2007;Sun et al. 2007).

proposal.statement: When fire propagation is slow (10 m/min or less), a single vehicle can serve several fire sites efficiently.
proposal.passage: When the fire propagation rate is slow (V F <= 10 m/min), the commanders may send resources to several fire sites via one vehicle (Fig. 2) (Zhang 2007;Sun et al. 2007).
proposal.impact_mechanism: slow fire spread allows one vehicle to serve multiple sites
proposal.impact_outcome: maintains suppression efficiency while reducing vehicle use

statements.verbatim_passage: The shortest time required for putting out the fire at a single site is found to be 19.3 h. Compared with the actual period of 2 months, the optimized resource allocation and transportation scheme is much more efficient, albeit higher in cost.
statements.passage_as_proposed: The shortest time required for putting out the fire at a single site is found to be 19.3 h. Compared with the actual period of 2 months, the optimized resource allocation and transportation scheme is much more efficient, albeit higher in cost.

proposal.statement: Optimizing the allocation and routing of suppression resources based on fire propagation rates can substantially shorten the time needed to extinguish wildfires.
proposal.passage: The shortest time required for putting out the fire at a single site is found to be 19.3 h. Compared with the actual period of 2 months, the optimized resource allocation and transportation scheme is much more efficient, albeit higher in cost.
proposal.impact_mechanism: optimized allocation and routing based on propagation rates
